sentences.text: Marta wants to know the status of her ticket, but the tickets live in another system, outside the agent.
The service manager wants the agent to check by itself.
Valeria has the answer: the Send H T T P request node.
It lets a topic call an A P I on the internet, like asking another system for a piece of data by message.
Nexo gets a courier badge.
Think of a letter leaving the mail room.
You type the endpoint address, the U R L.
You choose the method: get, post, patch, put, or delete.
You add headers if needed, such as Authorization.
Then you define the body, what goes inside the envelope.
By default the body is No Content, which is typical for a get.
When there is something to send, the body has two kinds of content.
With J S O N content, you send a J S O N object, typical for post or put.
With Edit J S O N and Formula, you write it as a Power F X object that uses variables.
With Raw content, you send a text string, also written with a Power F X formula.
The other system answers with a reply letter.
In Response data type, Valeria pastes a sample J S O N and chooses Get schema from sample J S O N.
Copilot Studio generates a variable with that shape, so the topic knows the fields of the reply.
In Save user response as, she chooses where to store it.

scenes.title: Decide: the body of a get

sentences.text: Your turn.
Valeria adds the node to read one ticket.
She uses get and leaves the body as it is.
What does the body hold by default?
An object with the ticket data?
No Content, nothing is sent?
Or a text string with the ticket?
Decide before I answer.
No Content, nothing is sent.
The body is No Content by default, which is typical for a get.
A J S O N object is for post or put, and a text string is Raw content.
Sometimes the letter comes back unanswered.
By default the node uses Raise an error.
The agent stops, and the On Error system topic fires.
The rest of the topic does not run.
Many authors leave this default and then do not understand why On Error appears.
Valeria wants a calmer path for Contoso.
With Continue on error, the node does not stop the agent.
The status code and the error body are saved in variables, and the topic goes on.
The error is of type Any, so you convert it with a Parse value node.
One more setting to know: the default request timeout is thirty seconds.
Your turn.
Marta asks about a missing ticket, and the tickets A P I fails.
The service manager wants the topic to reply and go on.
What should Valeria choose in Error handling?
Keep the default, Raise an error?
Set a longer request timeout?
Or switch to Continue on error?
Decide before I answer.
Switch to Continue on error.
It saves the status code and the error body in variables, and the topic goes on.
The default, Raise an error, stops the agent and fires On Error.

scenes.title: The Contoso case: find a ticket

sentences.text: Contoso queries its tickets A P I with a get.
The body stays as No Content, and the response is saved in a variable built from a sample J S O N.
Contoso chose Continue on error, so if the A P I returns a four oh four, the code goes into Topic Status Code and the error body into Topic Error Response.
The topic replies, I could not find that ticket, without stopping.
To create tickets, Contoso uses a post with J S O N content.
Here are the steps in Copilot Studio.
Open a topic and select Add node.
Point to Advanced and choose Send H T T P request.
Type the U R L and choose get.
Select Edit in Headers and body.
In Response data type, choose From sample data and paste a sample J S O N.
In Save user response as, create a variable.
In Error handling, choose Continue on error and define the status and error variables.
Your turn.
Valeria chose Continue on error, so the error body waits in a variable.
It is of type Any, and she wants its fields.
Which node converts it into a structured record?
Parse value, into a record?
Send a message, as plain text?
Or the On Error system topic?
Decide before I answer.
Parse value, into a record.
Parse value converts a value of type Any into a structured record the topic can use.
On Error only runs when an error is not handled, so it converts nothing.
Back in the mail room, Marta's question now gets an answer, even when the ticket does not exist.
Remember three things.
The node sends a letter with an address, a method, headers, and a body that is No Content by default.
Raise an error is the default, and it fires On Error.
Continue on error saves the status and the error body, and Parse value reads it.
